facts.statement: Timurlengia lived during the early Late Cretaceous (Turonian age) in the Kyzylkum Desert of Uzbekistan.
facts.quote: Timurlengia is an extinct genus of tyrannosauroid dinosaurs known from the early Late Cretaceous (Turonian age) Bissekty Formation of the Kyzylkum Desert in Uzbekistan.

facts.statement: The species Timurlengia euotica was named and described in 2016 by Brusatte, Averianov, Sues, Muir, and Butler.
facts.quote: In 2016, Stephen L. Brusatte, Alexander Averianov, Hans-Dieter Sues, Amy Muir, and Ian B. Butler named and described the type species Timurlengia euotica.

facts.statement: The genus name Timurlengia honors Timurlenk, the founder of the Timurid Empire in Central Asia.
facts.quote: The genus is named after Timurlenk, founder of the Timurid Empire in Central Asia.

facts.statement: The specific name euotica means "well-eared" because CT scans revealed a well-developed inner ear adapted for hearing low-frequency sounds.
facts.quote: The specific name euotica is Greek for "well-eared", because detailed CT scans show that Timurlengia had a well-developed inner ear for hearing low-frequency sounds.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was a subadult approximately 3 to 4 meters long and weighing 170 to 270 kilograms.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen belongs to a subadult about 3 - 4 m long and weighing around 170 - 270 kg.

facts.statement: The basioccipital bone has very short basal tubers that reach only one-third the height of the occipital condyle.
facts.quote: The basioccipital has very short basal tubers, only attaining a third of the height of the occipital condyle.

facts.statement: Timurlengia was likely a pursuit hunter capable of hearing low-frequency sounds due to the shape of its ear canal.
facts.quote: Timurlengia was likely a pursuit hunter that could hear low-frequency sounds based on the shape of its ear canal.

facts.statement: Hans-Dieter Sues hypothesized that tyrannosaurs developed advanced head features before large body size, a pattern supported by Timurlengia's braincase.
facts.quote: The braincase of Timurlengia shows that tyrannosaurs likely developed their advanced head first, as hypothesised by Hans-Dieter Sues, one of the fossil's describers.

facts.statement: Timurlengia possessed a long cochlear duct equal in height to the labyrinth, an adaptation for hearing low-frequency sounds.
facts.quote: Timurlengia has a long cochlear duct, with the same height as the labyrinth, an adaptation to hearing low-frequency sounds.

facts.statement: The robustness of Timurlengia's semicircular inner ear canals may have contributed to greater agility.
facts.quote: The robustness of the semicircular inner ear canals might be related to greater agility.

facts.statement: Timurlengia was likely a pursuit hunter equipped with blade-like teeth for slicing meat.
facts.quote: Based on the known material, Timurlengia was likely a pursuit hunter with blade-like teeth for slicing through meat.

facts.statement: Timurlengia is classified in the Tyrannosauroidea in a basal position, possibly as a sister species to Xiongguanlong.
facts.quote: Timurlengia was placed in the Tyrannosauroidea, in a basal position, as a possible sister species of Xiongguanlong.

facts.statement: Timurlengia was found in Uzbekistan within the Bissekty Formation of the Kyzylkum Desert, dating to the Turonian age of the mid-Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Fue encontrado en Uzbekistán, en la formación Bissekty en el desierto de Kyzyl Kum, procedente de la edad Turoniense a mediados del Cretácico.

facts.statement: It is debated whether specimen ZIN PH 2330/16 belongs to Timurlengia, as Voris et al. (2025) suggested it might be a dromaeosaurid instead.
facts.quote: However, specimen ZIN PH 2330/16 was suggested to be a dromaeosaurid instead by Voris et al. (2025).

facts.statement: The genus name Timurlengia is derived from the conqueror Timur Leng, founder of the Timurid Empire in Central Asia.
facts.quote: El nombre del género se deriva del conquistador Timur Leng, fundador del Imperio Timúrida en Asia Central.

facts.statement: Isolated tyrannosauroid bones from the Bissekty Formation were first described by Soviet researchers starting in 1944.
facts.quote: Desde 1944 en adelante, se ha descrito material de tiranosauroideos consistente de huesos aislados en la Formación Bissekty por investigadores soviéticos.

facts.statement: A neurocranium recovered in 2004 served as an anchor for neck muscles and protected the brain and ear canals.
facts.quote: En 2004 un equipo recuperó un neurocráneo, el cual habría servido de anclaje para los músculos del cuello del dinosaurio y protegido su cerebro y los canales de sus oídos.

facts.statement: The neurocranium was identified as a new species by Steve Brusatte in 2014 after being stored at the Zoological Institute of the Russian Academy of Sciences.
facts.quote: El neurocráneo fue depositado en un gabinete en el Instituto Zoológico de la Academia Rusa de Ciencias, hasta que el experto en tiranosáuridos Steve Brusatte lo identificó como una nueva especie en 2014.

facts.statement: Additional fossils referred to the species include ZIN PH 854/16, a right half of a neurocranium, and ZIN PH 676/16, a right maxilla.
facts.quote: Estos incluyen los especímenes ZIN PH 854/16, una la mitad derecha de un neurocráneo, ZIN PH 676/16, un maxilar derecho.

facts.statement: These fossils were assigned to the species based on the assumption that only one tyrannosauroid taxon existed in the Bissekty Formation.
facts.quote: Estos fósiles fueron referidos a la especie asumiendo que solo había un taxón de tiranosauroideo presente en la Formación Bissekty.

facts.statement: Timurlengia is placed in the superfamily Tyrannosauroidea in a basal position as a possible sister taxon to Xiongguanlong.
facts.quote: Timurlengia fue situado en la superfamilia Tyrannosauroidea en una posición basal, como un posible taxón hermano de Xiongguanlong.

facts.statement: Together they appear to represent a clade of long-snouted forms that could be the group closest to the family Tyrannosauridae.
facts.quote: Juntos parecen representar un clado de formas de hocico largo que podría ser el grupo más cercano a la familia Tyrannosauridae.

facts.statement: The discovery of Timurlengia filled a gap in the fossil record between small marginal hunters and large superpredators.
facts.quote: El descubrimiento de Timurlengia ha llenado este vacío.

facts.statement: Timurlengia reveals that tyrannosaurs had not yet reached giant size but had already evolved key brain and sensory traits found in Late Cretaceous giants.
facts.quote: Timurlengia revela que los tiranosaurios aún tenían que alcanzar el tamaño gigantesco en aquella época pero ya habían evolucionado características claves del cerebro y los sentidos propios de las grandes especies del final del Cretácico.

facts.statement: Tyrannosaurs apparently developed large size rapidly during the Late Cretaceous, with their success as superpredators possibly facilitated by brains and senses that evolved initially in small bodies.
facts.quote: Los tiranosaurios aparentemente desarrollaron el gran tamaño rápidamente durante el final del Cretácico, y su éxito en el nicho del superdepredador puede haber sido facilitado por su cerebro y sus agudos sentidos los cuales evolucionaron inicialmente en un tamaño corporal reducido.

facts.statement: The neurocranium suggests tyrannosaurs likely developed advanced heads first, a hypothesis proposed by describer Hans-Dieter Sues.
facts.quote: El neurocráneo de Timurlengia muestra que los tiranosaurios probablemente desarrollaron su avanzada cabeza en primer lugar, como fue hipotetizado por Hans-Dieter Sues, uno de los descriptores del fósil.

facts.statement: Although much smaller than Tyrannosaurus, the Timurlengia skull shows a sophisticated brain that likely provided keen sight, smell, and hearing.
facts.quote: El cráneo de Timurlengia, aunque mucho más pequeño que el de Tyrannosaurus, muestra un cerebro sofisticado que debió brindarle una vista, olfato y oído agudos.

facts.statement: The Timurlengia head is far less pneumatized than in large tyrannosaurids, suggesting air spaces in later species may have lightened the skull or aided hearing despite larger size.
facts.quote: La cabeza de Timurlengia está mucho menos neumatizada que la de los grandes tiranosáuridos; los espacios con aire mayores en las especies tardías podrían haber sido una adaptación para aligerar el cráneo o para mantener un buen sentido del oído a pesar del mayor tamaño.

facts.statement: Timurlengia was likely a pursuit predator with knife-shaped teeth for cutting through meat, based on preserved remains.
facts.quote: Timurlengia era probablemente un depredador de persecución con dientes en forma de cuchillo para cortar a través de la carne, basándose en sus restos preservados.

facts.statement: The robustness of the inner ear semicircular canals may be related to great agility.
facts.quote: La robustez de los canales semicirculares del oído interno puede estar relacionada con una gran agilidad.

facts.statement: Timurlengia had a long cochlear duct, same height as the labyrinth, an adaptation for hearing low-frequency sounds.
facts.quote: Timurlengia tenía un largo conducto de la cóclea, con la misma altura que el laberinto, una adaptación para oír sonidos de baja frecuencia.

facts.statement: This may indicate the animal used low-frequency calls to communicate with other members of its species.
facts.quote: Esto bien podría indicar que este animal usaba llamados de baja frecuencia para comunicarse con otros miembros de su especie.

facts.statement: The time range for Timurlengia is the Turonian stage, from 93.9 to 89.8 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Turonian to Turonian (93.9 to 89.8 million years ago)

facts.statement: The parent group for Timurlengia is Tyrannosauroidea.
facts.quote: Parent group: Tyrannosauroidea

facts.statement: Timurlengia is classified in the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia
